facts.fact: Reporting ART's 2024 Annual Observatory, TechAfrica News says transport, mainly by the incumbent CAMTEL, relies on a national fibre optic network of nearly 12,000 km; no regions or towns are named.

ITWeb Africa reports that in 2023 the government transferred to Camtel an overhead fibre-optic network of about 812km on electricity poles along the southern interconnected grid, which serves major cities including Douala and Yaounde, adding to Camtel's terrestrial fibre network of about 12,000km.
Camtel's national fibre-optic backbone, about 12,000 km, serves all ten regional capitals and 51 of 58 divisional capitals, according to the ART report quoted by Ecomatin.
The ART report says Camtel's transport network revenue rose with demand for bandwidth from mobile operators, ISPs and businesses.
OBS-CC says over 12,000 km of fibre form the national backbone run by Camtel, linking the regions to each other and to the coast, with published estimates up to nearly 16,000 km.
OBS-CC says Camtel carries Chad's traffic to the sea cables over its fibre, and that a 15 May 2025 deal settling Sotel Tchad's debt raised that capacity to over 100 Gbit/s.

note: Cameroon's commitment on the Nana-Mbere segment is not a contract or works begun.

facts.fact: CAMTEL's 2026 product sheet says its national fibre-optic network of nearly 10,000 km covers the whole territory and carries its inter-city leased lines on the national backbone.
CAMTEL's 2026 product sheet offers operators and ISPs inter-city leased lines (LLI) on its national backbone, IP transit and cross-connection, as wholesale products.

Cameroon's telecoms regulator ART says its audit, nearly complete, of the 112 sections of CAMTEL's national fibre-optic network, which link operators' sites across regions, departments and districts, found significant degradation with recurrent cuts and partly unavailable sections.
Digital Business Africa reports that Camtel, the national operator, makes dark fibre available to MTN Cameroon under a contract, and that the regulator ART proposes dark fibre access.
Camtel said in a statement of 16 November 2026 that BB4, the three-year fourth phase of Cameroon's national fibre-optic backbone costed at CFA148 billion, had been launched.
The regulator ART's audit of 112 sections of the national backbone, reported 10 November 2026, found disruptions on in-service routes including Edea-Yaounde, Douala-Limbe and Bamenda-Bafoussam.

ITWeb Africa reports Camtel saying Phase IV of the national backbone expansion has been launched after presidential approval of financing, a three-year programme with a budget of 148 billion CFA francs.

ITWeb Africa reports that MTN Cameroon and Orange Cameroun rely largely on Camtel's backbone for data transmission and interconnection, and Camtel says private operators have access to its dark fibre at prices below cost.

note: Says only that the backbone is solely managed by Camtel and has deteriorated; no region reach or lease terms stated.
The plan lists oversight of the national fibre backbone as a programme; no build, service or reach is stated.
